dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise, good afternoon.
Hello, yes. Good afternoon. I am calling about, um, the drain. The storm drain, in the street. It is, it is not taking the water.
Okay, sorry to hear that. Which street is it on? Whereabouts?
Yes, so, the water comes from the next street, up the hill. It [pause] it runs down, all the way down, and goes straight into my yard. Into the, the front, where the [line breaks up] parking.
I'm sorry, you broke up on me a little. The water comes down the hill from the next street and into your yard, is that right?
Yes, yes, exactly. Down the hill. Every time it rains hard, same thing. And this time, with the rain Wednesday into Thursday, the big one, yesterday it finished, it was very bad.
Yeah, that was a soaker. We had a lot of calls on it. Is the drain at the bottom of the hill, near your property?
Near, yes. Is full. Is full of leaves, the, the [inaudible] on top. The water cannot go in, so it goes around, and then it comes to me.
Got it, so the grate's clogged with leaves and debris. Is it still standing there today, or has it drained down some?
Today is less. But still there is a, a pond. And the cars, they are going very slow through it. Like a crawl. Nobody wants to splash, so the traffic, it stops, it backs up. In front of my business.

Okay. That's a safety issue too, then, with cars crawling through. What I'll need is the exact location so the crew can find the right drain. Can you give me the street and a number nearby, or a cross street?

Ah. [pause] I would like not to give the address now. I am calling from the car, the phone is, the signal is bad. Can you, can you just put it, the drain, to be cleaned? It is a, how you say, a simple thing.

I understand, and I do want to get it cleaned, but without a location the crew can't tell which drain it is. There are a lot of them on a hill like that. Is there a cross street, or a landmark you can tell me?
[crosstalk] Sorry, say again?
I said, can you tell me a cross street or a landmark? Something the crew can look for.
Hm. [line breaks up] it is the street at the bottom, where the hill finishes. Is a, a corner. The water makes a turn there. I can, I can call you back with the name when I am home. Is that okay?
That works. Or you can give me your number now and I'll put in the request with what you've told me, and someone can call you to confirm the spot. Would that be easier?
Yes, yes, better. My number is four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-nine.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-nine. And your name?
Antonio Medeiros. M-E-D-E-I-R-O-S.

Thank you, Mr. Medeiros. So I have a clogged storm drain at the bottom of a hill, water running down from the next street into your yard, traffic slowing to a crawl, and a request to have it cleaned. I'll note that you're going to confirm the street.
Yes. Thank you. And, um, this is not the first time. Every year, the same. The leaves come, nobody cleans, and then the rain. I think, the city, it should look before the storm, not after.
I hear you, and I'll put that in the notes too. After a storm like this the crews are stretched thin, but a clogged drain with traffic backing up goes toward the top of the list.
Okay. When, when they come? Today?
I can't promise today. It could be today, it could be early next week, depending on what else came in. If it starts rising again, or a car stalls out in it, call right back and say it's urgent.
Okay, okay. I understand. I only [pause] I have to go now, honestly. The school, the bake sale is today, Friday, and we have not baked. Nothing. My wife is going to, [inaudible] me.
Well, then you'd better get moving. Go get some cookies from somewhere. I'll get this logged right now.
Yes, yes, from the store, maybe. Thank you, Denise. Please, the drain.
I've got it. Drive safe, Mr. Medeiros. Bye now.
Goodbye.
